newDescription:
In this Year 3 English lesson, pupils learn how subordinating conjunctions create subordinate clauses and how those clauses can be positioned and punctuated within sentences.

This lesson includes:
✔ Revisiting independent clauses and subordinate clauses
✔ Understanding that a clause contains a subject and a verb
✔ Recognising that an independent clause makes complete sense on its own
✔ Recognising that a subordinate clause depends on an independent clause
✔ Identifying subordinate clauses at the beginning, middle and end of sentences
✔ Using commas when subordinate clauses come first or provide extra information in the middle
✔ Learning how subordinating conjunctions link clauses together
✔ Using conjunctions such as if, since, as, when, although, while, after, before, until and because
✔ Using phrases such as so that and just as to introduce subordinate clauses
✔ Creating subordinate clauses to add time, reason, condition, contrast or purpose
✔ Choosing suitable subordinating conjunctions for sentence meaning
✔ Identifying main clauses and subordinate clauses in context
✔ Moving subordinate clauses to different positions while preserving meaning
✔ Revising word classes alongside clause structure
✔ Applying punctuation accurately when clause order changes

Pupils begin by revisiting the difference between independent and subordinate clauses and exploring where subordinate clauses can appear within a sentence. They learn how comma use changes depending on clause position.

The lesson then develops pupils' use of subordinating conjunctions through sentence-building activities. They practise joining ideas with conjunctions that express time, reason, condition, purpose and contrast, and identify the subordinate clause created by each conjunction.

A series of interactive activities gives repeated practice in selecting conjunctions, writing subordinate clauses and distinguishing between main and subordinate clauses. Pupils also create their own sentences from prompts and play word-based games to reinforce the conjunctions.

Later tasks combine clause work with wider SPaG knowledge. Pupils identify word classes, locate subordinate clauses, move those clauses to the beginning of sentences and add commas where required.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to identify and create subordinate clauses using a range of subordinating conjunctions, position clauses flexibly, and punctuate them accurately.
